correctness.rationale: With edges labeled \(c\), \(p_i\), \(q_i\), and \(r_i\), the \(q_i\) form a simplex. Any matching containing \(c\) blocks no \(q_i\); otherwise it contains at most one \(p_i\) and at most one \(r_j\), so at most two indices are blocked. For \(n\ge 3\), an unblocked \(q_k\) exists, placing the matching in \(\operatorname{st}(q_k)\); hence the entire flag matching complex is the collapsible star cluster of \(Q\). The cases \(n=1\) and \(n=2\) are proved directly, and exact enumeration through \(n=7\) reproduces all boundary and homology checks.

evidence: Donovan–Scoville computes Dutch windmills, whose cycles meet at one vertex; this does not specialize to cycles sharing an edge.

Bayer–Jelić Milutinović–Vega define polygonal line tilings so that no three polygons intersect. Every quadrilateral book with \(n\ge 3\) violates that hypothesis because all pages share the common edge.
The outerplanar matching-complex theorem does not cover \(n\ge 3\): three page paths already exhibit a subdivision of \(K_{2,3}\), so the books are nonouterplanar.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The natural stronger-looking families were checked by hypotheses rather than title similarity. Their hypotheses fail precisely in the new infinite range \(n\ge 3\).

originality.rationale: The claim is the exact ordinary-matching-complex classification of edge-sharing quadrilateral books, with simplicial collapsibility for all \(n\ge 3\). The closest inspected sources concern vertex-sharing Dutch windmills, polygonal line tilings with a no-three-intersections condition, or all outerplanar graphs. None implies the \(n\ge 3\) book classification; small \(n\) may be contained in broader known classes and is not the originality basis.
residual_risks: The terminology 'book graph' is not uniform; an equivalent edge-amalgamated-cycle result could be catalogued under a different name.

The \(n=2\) boundary case may be subsumed by polygonal-line-tiling formulas. The originality assessment therefore rests on the exact \(n\ge 3\) collapsibility theorem and sharp transition, not on novelty of each boundary value.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a sharp structural transition in a natural infinite graph family: nontrivial matching-complex homotopy at one and two pages disappears by an explicit simplicial collapse at three pages and stays collapsed thereafter. The blocked-index proof is reusable, and the \(n\ge 3\) examples are nonouterplanar, so the result is not merely a special case of the broad outerplanar wedge theorem.
